mechanics.name: Teamwork: Collective Stealth
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever another Survivor finishes healing you, both you and that Survivor who healed you suppress Scratch Marks while within 8/12/16 m of one another. The effect lingers for 4 seconds after leaving range and resumes if you re-enter range before the linger ends. Survivors can only be affected by one instance of Teamwork: Collective Stealth at a time.
activation: Another Survivor must finish healing you.
Both Survivors must remain within 8/12/16 m to keep the shared effect active.
Ends/deactivates when: The effect ends 4 seconds after leaving range unless you re-enter before the timer ends.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (unknown): No material live balance change could be verified from available patch history.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After another Survivor heals you, both of you hide Scratch Marks while staying close together.
duration: Continues while within range; lingers for 4 seconds after leaving range.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: A Survivor can be affected by only one instance of this perk at a time.
specialInteractions: The effect applies to both the healed Survivor and the Survivor who healed them.

editorial.summary: After another Survivor finishes healing you, both of you suppress Scratch Marks while you remain within up to 16 metres of each other.
useCases: Leave a healing area together without advertising either Survivor's sprint trail.
Use the linger to split briefly before deciding whether to re-enter the tether.
Pair with Blood Pact or other two-person movement builds.
counters: Requires another Survivor to heal you fully.
The effect demands close proximity after the heal.
Grouping two Survivors can reduce generator spread and invite multi-target pressure.
pros: No fixed duration while the tether remains active.
Useful immediately after a vulnerable healing interaction.
cons: Scratch Marks are only one tracking channel.
Solo Q teammates rarely cooperate with the proximity requirement.
analysis: Teamwork: Collective Stealth ranks this position because suppressing two Survivors' Scratch Marks can create a clean rotation after a heal, but the perk asks them to remain close enough that the Killer may pressure both at once.

The no-duration design is interesting. As long as the pair respects the range, the stealth continues, and the brief linger allows momentary separation. A coordinated duo can deliberately move through indoor structures without leaving the normal trail.

Macro pressure is the problem. Survivors usually want to heal and then split toward different objectives. Collective Stealth rewards the opposite behavior, making its strongest state inherently expensive.
This is another Teamwork perk whose ceiling belongs to premades. In Solo Q, the other player usually runs away with their own plan before you have a chance to exploit the effect.
editorial.verdict: A functional two-person stealth tether with an awkward macro cost. Collective Stealth works when staying together is already the plan, and fights the game when it is not.
